summary: Our project consists of developing a web application based on a probabilistic model that allows us to identify the crops with the greatest suitability for the environmental and soil conditions of a region. The platform will integrate information provided by farmers, such as the location of the land, water availability, source of supply, planting month and irrigation system. These data will be complemented with information from NASA SMAP, MODIS and POWER, as well as databases with data from soilGrids, INEGI, SIAP and FAO. By analyzing climatic, hydrological, and soil variables and comparing them against the specific requirements of each crop the probability of encountering favorable conditions for crop development will be estimated, and potential limiting factors will be identified. The objective is to provide agricultural recommendations based on scientific data that facilitate crop selection, optimize the use of natural resources, and contribute to the adaptation of agricultural activities in the face of climate variability and change.
details: The mobile application will work through a system of collection, integration and analysis of geospatial and agricultural information. Initially, the user will provide information about their land, including geographical details, the crop of interest, water availability, water source, sowing month and irrigation system. Based on the coordinates provided, the platform will retrieve information from various sources, such as NASA SMAP, MODIS and POWER, SoilGrids, INEGI, SIAP and FAO. The data obtained will enable the identification of the region’s climatic, hydrological and soil conditions, as well as historical production records and the specific requirements of each crop. Subsequently, the variables will be organised and processed to establish relationships between the land’s characteristics and the agronomic needs of the selected crops. This information will be used by a probabilistic model to assess the environmental suitability of each crop and estimate the likelihood of finding favourable conditions for its growth. Finally, the application will present the results through indicators, comparisons and recommendations, identifying the most suitable crops and any potential limiting environmental factors. The aim is thus to provide a tool to support crop selection and the adaptation of agricultural activities in the face of climate variability.
